chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Al-Minqari, from Sufyan ibn Uyayna, who said:
I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Advising for the sake of Allah among His creatures is upon you, for you will not meet Him with a deed superior to it.'

key_terms.النُّصْحِ: Sincere advice, goodwill, or devotion to the benefit of others

ai.seo_question: What is the most superior deed according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elevates 'al-nush' (sincere counsel and goodwill) to the status of the supreme deed, suggesting its comprehensive nature encompasses all other acts of worship. This concept is central to Shia ethics, where advising the creation with pure intent is viewed as a manifestation of divine love and a means of spiritual perfection. The emphasis on sincerity (ikhlas) in directing this advice to Allah's creatures highlights the interconnectedness of vertical devotion and horizontal social responsibility.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Qasim Bin Muhammad, from Al Minqary, from Sufyan Bin Uyayna who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Upon you is with the advising for the Sake of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> among His<sup>azwj</sup> creatures, for you will never (be able to) meet Him<sup>azwj</sup> with a deed more superior than it’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from al-Minqari from Sufyan ibn ‘Uyaynah who has said the following: “
I heard abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) saying, ‘You must provide good advice for the sake of Allah to His creatures; you will not meet Him with any good deed better than this.’”
